cases.sentence: Но стòит подняться буре, взволноваться морю и двинуться ___, и тогда уж заблуждение невозможно.
cases.explain: «самому кораблю» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: In quiet and untroubled times it seems to every administrator that it is only by his efforts that the whole population under his rule is kept going, and in this consciousness of being indispensable every administrator finds the chief reward of his labor and efforts. While the sea of history remains calm the ruler-administrator in his frail bark, holding on with a boat hook to the ship of the people and himself moving, naturally imagines that his efforts move the ship he is holding on to. But as soon as a storm arises and the sea begins to heave and the ship to move, such a delusion is no longer possible. The ship moves independently with its own enormous motion, the boat hook no longer reaches the moving vessel, and suddenly the administrator, instead of appearing a ruler and a source of power, becomes an insignificant, useless, feeble man.

cases.sentence: Оба были бледны, и полицеймейстер, передав об исполнении своего поручения, сообщил, что на дворе графа стояла ___ народа, желавшего его видеть.
cases.explain: «огромная толпа» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The superintendent of police, whom the crowd had stopped, went in to see him at the same time as an adjutant who informed the count that the horses were harnessed. They were both pale, and the superintendent of police, after reporting that he had executed the instructions he had received, informed the count that an immense crowd had collected in the courtyard and wished to see him.

cases.sentence: Растопчин, ни слова не отвечая, встал и ___ направился в свою роскошную, светлую гостиную, подошел к двери балкона, взялся за ручку, оставил ее и перешел к окну, из которого виднее была вся толпа.
cases.explain: «быстрыми шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Without saying a word Rostopchín rose and walked hastily to his light, luxurious drawing room, went to the balcony door, took hold of the handle, let it go again, and went to the window from which he had a better view of the whole crowd. The tall lad was standing in front, flourishing his arm and saying something with a stern look. The bloodstained smith stood beside him with a gloomy face. A drone of voices was audible through the closed window.

cases.sentence: Высокий малый стоял в ___ и с строгим лицом, размахивая рукой, говорил что-то.
cases.explain: «передних рядах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.

cases.explain: «мрачным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.explain: «буйная толпа» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Your excellency, they say they have got ready, according to your orders, to go against the French, and they shouted something about treachery. But it is a turbulent crowd, your excellency—I hardly managed to get away from it. Your excellency, I venture to suggest …” “You may go. I don’t need you to tell me what to do!” exclaimed Rostopchín angrily.

cases.sentence: Как это часто бывает с ___, гнев уже владел им, но он искал еще для него предмета.
cases.explain: «горячими людьми» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: He stood by the balcony door looking at the crowd. “This is what they have done with Russia! This is what they have done with me!” thought he, full of an irrepressible fury that welled up within him against the someone to whom what was happening might be attributed. As often happens with passionate people, he was mastered by anger but was still seeking an object on which to vent it. “Here is that mob, the dregs of the people,” he thought as he gazed at the crowd: “this rabble they have roused by their folly! They want a victim,” he thought as he looked at the tall lad flourishing his arm. And this thought occurred to him just because he himself desired a victim, something on which to vent his rage.

cases.explain: «другой раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Is the carriage ready?” he asked again.

cases.sentence: Через несколько минут из ___ поспешно вышел офицер, приказал что-то, и драгуны вытянулись.
cases.explain: «парадных дверей» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: A few minutes later an officer came hurriedly out of the front door, gave an order, and the dragoons formed up in line. The crowd moved eagerly from the balcony toward the porch. Rostopchín, coming out there with quick angry steps, looked hastily around as if seeking someone.

cases.sentence: ___ этот был одет в щегольской когда-то, крытый синим сукном, потертый лисий тулупчик и в грязные посконные арестантские шаровары, засунутые в нечищенные, стоптанные тонкие сапоги.
cases.explain: «Молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Where is he?” he inquired. And as he spoke he saw a young man coming round the corner of the house between two dragoons. He had a long thin neck, and his head, that had been half shaved, was again covered by short hair. This young man was dressed in a threadbare blue cloth coat lined with fox fur, that had once been smart, and dirty hempen convict trousers, over which were pulled his thin, dirty, trodden-down boots. On his thin, weak legs were heavy chains which hampered his irresolute movements.
